overhead.note: the profiler’s own CPU frames and its share of the GC pauses, taken out of every number in this report: each run loses exactly what fell inside it; the start-up scan of compiled code and the final reads sit outside the runs. The sampler’s own thread and the inspector’s are not visible from inside and are not taken out.

findings.message: Over 2537 ms the CPU was busy 41% and 25 outbound network calls took 395 ms combined.
Of the 789 ms render: load functions 19.4 ms + 369 ms waiting · other 270 ms · component render 62.1 ms · remote functions 0.00 ms + 39.5 ms waiting.

3 calls ran one after another for 111 ms: GET 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/pricing, GET 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/inventory, timer · rows (routes/hell/+page.server.ts:13). Started together they would cost 59.8 ms — about 51.6 ms saved.
findings.fix: Start them together (Promise.all) when they are independent; a call that needs an earlier result stays sequential.

findings.message: 16 calls to 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/product/:id — one per item, 112 ms together.
findings.fix: Batch them: one request with the ids (or a bulk endpoint), or fetch the list with its children included.

findings.message: Biggest CPU consumer: @ionic/core (415 ms, 40.8% of busy time).
Most expensive component: Root at 191 ms total.

ds.render ran 242 times in one render (lib/hell/ds-ssr.ts:46), together: 175 ms of wall for 22478 ms of summed work, 92.1 ms each. Most of it is tag ion-chip: 96 of them, 175 ms of wall (8148 ms summed).
findings.fix: They already overlap, so batching gains little: the cost is each one (make it cheaper, or cache it) and how many there are (render fewer).

findings.message: ds.pass took 245 ms of the render (ds_ssr (lib/hell/ds-ssr.ts:225)).
findings.fix: The profiler cannot see inside it — this is the wait to take to whoever owns that service, or to cache.

findings.message: ds.render.all took 176 ms of the render (processDsTags (lib/hell/ds-ssr.ts:38)).
findings.fix: The profiler cannot see inside it — this is the wait to take to whoever owns that service, or to cache.

findings.message: stock.lookup ran 16 times in one render (load (routes/hell/+page.server.ts:79)), 114 ms together, 7.05 ms each. Most of it is key P0: 1 of them, 7.53 ms of wall.
findings.fix: Once per item is the N+1 shape: batch it (one call for all the ids), or fetch the parent with its children included.

findings.message: ogygia added 11.1 ms to the render: 52 islands, seed 255 KB, props 126 KB, remote seed 164 B.
The page seed is 255 KB: an island reads $page, so that much of page.data ships to the browser and is serialized on every render.
findings.fix: Read only the keys the island needs (page.data.x, not page.data) so seed shaping trims it, or pass the values as props.

findings.message: PriceTicker, ProductCard read page.data whole, so every key ships in the seed (255 KB, the biggest is catalog at 225 KB).
findings.fix: Read the keys by name (page.data.catalog, not a spread or a loop over page.data) so seed shaping can drop the rest, or pass the values in as props.

findings.message: The seed (255 KB) left the JSON lane because of catalog.facets (Map) — devalue writes and revives it several times slower than JSON.parse.
findings.fix: Send that value as a plain string or number (a Date as toISOString(), a Map as an object), or keep it out of page.data.

findings.message: MegaHeader's props (111 KB) use devalue because of config.updated (Date).
findings.fix: JSON props parse on the fast lane in the browser: pass the value as a string or number, or derive it inside the island.

findings.message: ProductCard has 48 copies on the page, each waking on visible with its own 80 B of props.
findings.fix: One island around the list hydrates once; or wake: 'interaction' so a copy pays only when touched.

findings.message: routes/hell/+page.server.ts started only after routes/hell/+layout.server.ts finished (65.8 ms later) — Kit runs a page load and its layout loads together unless the page awaits parent().
findings.fix: Move the await parent() below the page's own fetches (start them first, await parent() after), or pass what the page needs some other way — the two loads then overlap.

findings.message: routes/hell/+layout.ts is a universal load: on this render it waited 24.9 ms on calls. On a page with the client router it runs again in the browser on every navigation, and its data must be serializable.
findings.fix: If it only needs the server (a database, a secret, a private API), rename it +layout.server.ts and the browser never runs it.

findings.message: ProductCard (island host) renders 48 ProductCard rows per render, 43.7 ms together (0.91 ms each).
findings.fix: The list is the cost, not the row: page it, window it, or defer the part below the fold into a hole.

findings.message: GET 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/session waited 45.6 ms; its own Server-Timing says SvelteKit render 45.4 ms, postgres 31.0 ms, render 9.00 ms — 85.4 ms of the wait is on their side, 0.00 ms is the network and their framework.
findings.fix: The wait is theirs: take the biggest entry to whoever owns that service, or cache the response.

findings.message: 9 hot functions sit on one path under processDsTags: fn @ ds-ssr.ts:42 · tags.map(async (tag) => {, insertStyleTags, setAttribute, fn @ index.mjs:54521 · __namespaceURI; and 5 more — 186 ms together (18.3% of busy).
findings.fix: Fix processDsTags once — call it less, cache what it computes, or move it out of the render — rather than each function on its own; the graph under "Paths to fix" shows the chain.

findings.message: 21 hot functions sit on one path under ProductCard: formatPrice, currencySymbol, Icon, structuredClone and 17 more — 128 ms together (12.5% of busy).
findings.fix: Fix ProductCard once — call it less, cache what it computes, or move it out of the render — rather than each function on its own; the graph under "Paths to fix" shows the chain.

findings.message: 2 hot functions sit on one path under sortCountries: collate, stripDiacritics — 17.9 ms together (1.8% of busy).
findings.fix: Fix sortCountries once — call it less, cache what it computes, or move it out of the render — rather than each function on its own; the graph under "Paths to fix" shows the chain.

findings.message: One render leaves 77.7 MB alive after a full collection: hydrateAppClosure via hydrateFactory (hydrate/index.mjs:12) (58.9 MB), match via extractStyleTags (hell/ds-ssr.ts:190) (3 MB), registerComponents via hydrateAppClosure (hydrate/index.mjs:171) (2.9 MB). Every render adds that much; the instance grows until it restarts.
findings.fix: Whatever holds these (a module-level cache, a registry, a closure kept by a long-lived object) must release them or be bounded. The sites named are where the kept objects were made; what keeps them is their owner.

findings.message: 24,120 promises per render. Each is an allocation and a microtask; at this volume they are a cost no single function shows. Mostly from: #collect_content_async (chunks/server.js:4030) 13%, drainQueue (hell/_page.server.ts.js:16) 12%, hydrateComponent (hydrate/index.mjs:5570) 10%.
findings.fix: Find the loop that awaits per item (a render per tag, a fetch per row) and do the work in one call, or on a plain array without async at all.

findings.message: toProductVM runs 48 times per render at 2.038 ms each (97.8 ms), allocating 43 KB per call. If its result depends only on its argument, a cache keyed on it runs it once per distinct value.
formatPrice runs 1200 times per render at 0.05 ms each (60.0 ms). If its result depends only on its argument, a cache keyed on it runs it once per distinct value.
53.5 ms of the 79.5 ms of GC is the garbage replace (called from (anonymous) (hell/ds-ssr.ts:61)) makes: 1771.3 MB of the 2633.7 MB allocated in the window (67%), across the window's 49 pauses.
findings.fix: Allocate less there: reuse the object between calls, avoid a clone or a JSON round trip of a large value, build strings once instead of in a loop. The heap also grew 23 MB over the window: something keeps what it allocates.

findings.message: 139.6 MB of the 319.8 MB the heap grew came in one 263 ms stretch (530.6 MB/s), while processDsTags ran — and a collection fell inside it, so the allocation was more than the growth shows.
findings.fix: Look at the allocators table for that stretch: the makers with a caller there are the ones filling the heap that fast.

findings.message: The render called its own server 13 times (/hell/api/session, /hell/api/pricing, /hell/api/inventory, …), 293 ms of requests answered by the same event loop that was rendering: the page waited on itself, and every one of those calls paid a full HTTP round trip to reach code in the same process.
findings.fix: Call the function behind the endpoint directly from the load (import it), or use a remote function; keep fetch for servers that are not this one.

findings.message: The event loop stalled up to 253 ms (p99) — long synchronous work blocks every other request.
Memory grew 144 MB during the window.
234 ms of busy time is the profiler itself — a one-time cost when recording starts. Your app did not pay this outside the recording.
